SourceDataAvailability.MediaWikiXml: Contains page/module Wikitext and historical Lua revisions; does not establish Cargo-owned table rows.
SourceDataAvailability.AuthorizedMediaWikiDatabase: NOT_INSPECTED_BY_CODEX; no production database access performed.
SourceDataAvailability.ContinuumWikiPersistence: Contains imported pages/revisions only; no authenticated historical Cargo snapshot established.

ProvenanceRules: Do not substitute current Cargo rows for rows that would have existed at a historical page revision.
A future comparison requires a versioned Cargo snapshot tied to the fixture and source revision timestamp.
Query source strings do not prove query results.

ProposedReadOnlyBoundary.Location: Trusted host, outside the Lua worker
ProposedReadOnlyBoundary.Interface: Typed CargoQueryRequest/CargoQueryResult with table, field, where, join, groupBy, orderBy, limit, source revision, and provenance fields
ProposedReadOnlyBoundary.Allowlisting: Explicit table and field allowlists derived from authenticated Cargo schema; reject unknown identifiers
ProposedReadOnlyBoundary.TransportAssessment: Existing one-shot worker protocol cannot safely perform an arbitrary host callback. Prefer host-side pre-resolution of approved query results in the request bundle, or an explicit bounded request/resume protocol with correlation, cancellation, and provenance; do not add an implicit SQL callback.

ImplementationStages: Obtain an authorized, read-only Cargo schema and versioned row snapshot tied to the MediaWiki reference capture.
Define typed allowlisted query plans for the observed tables/fields and validate them without SQL passthrough.
Add host-side deterministic result resolution and provenance-bearing worker data bundles.
Add negative tests for unknown tables/fields, unsupported joins/expressions, row/output/time limits, missing snapshots, and cancellation.
Capture independent MediaWiki references using the same historical Cargo dataset before claiming parity.
SecurityStatus: Preserved; this audit adds no database access, worker capability, production Lua authorization, or parser behavior.
